prompt.en: Which order matches how Noah tested whether the waters had gone down?

text.en: Dove that returned, raven, dove with an olive leaf, dove that stayed away
Raven, dove with an olive leaf, dove that returned, dove that stayed away
Raven, dove that returned, dove with an olive leaf, dove that stayed away
Dove with an olive leaf, raven, dove that returned, dove that stayed away

explanation.en: Noah first sent a raven, then a dove that found no resting place. Seven days later the dove brought an olive leaf, and after seven more days it did not return.

prompt.en: Why did Abram propose that he and Lot separate?

text.en: The land could not support both households, and their herdsmen fought
A famine had left too little food in Canaan for both households to share
God had commanded Abram to send Lot back to their relatives in Haran
Lot’s household had refused to worship at the altar Abram had built

explanation.en: Their possessions were too great for the land to bear, strife arose between the herdsmen, and Abram sought peace between relatives.

prompt.en: When Joseph revealed himself, what purpose did he tell his brothers lay behind his being in Egypt?

text.en: Pharaoh had needed a wise ruler to govern all of his household
His suffering had been a punishment that would test his brothers’ repentance
He had been taken there so Israel could later inherit the land of Egypt
God had sent him ahead of them to preserve life through the famine

explanation.en: Joseph told his brothers not to be grieved, because God had sent him before them to preserve life and save them by a great deliverance.

prompt.en: What did Yahweh say the blood on the houses would do on the night He struck Egypt?

text.en: Show the Egyptians which families belonged to the people of Israel
Serve as a token, so He would pass over and no plague would destroy them
Mark the households who would be first to leave Egypt the next morning
Consecrate each firstborn son of Israel for service at the altar of Yahweh

explanation.en: The blood was a token on the houses. When Yahweh saw it He would pass over, and no plague would destroy those inside.

prompt.en: What change did Moses’ father-in-law counsel so that Moses would not wear himself out?

text.en: Hear the people’s cases only on set days at the start of each month
Let Aaron and the seventy elders take over every case in his place
Appoint able judges; bring major cases to Moses
Send all disputes back to the head of each tribe to settle alone

explanation.en: He advised Moses to place able, God-fearing men over the people. They would judge small matters and bring great matters to Moses, sharing the load.

prompt.en: What reason does the Sabbath commandment in Exodus 20 itself give for keeping the seventh day holy?

text.en: Yahweh made heaven and earth in six days and rested on the seventh
Israel crossed through the sea and left Egypt behind on the seventh day
Yahweh gave the law to Moses at Sinai on the seventh day of the month
Manna did not fall on the seventh day, so no food could be gathered

explanation.en: The commandment grounds the Sabbath in creation: Yahweh made all things in six days and rested on the seventh, so He blessed that day and made it holy.

prompt.en: In Jesus’ explanation of the parable of the farmer, what do the thorns represent?

text.en: Hardship and persecution that make a new believer fall away
The evil one stealing the message before it is understood
False teachers who mix their own words with the truth
Worries and wealth crowding out the word

explanation.en: Jesus said the seed among thorns is one who hears the word, but worldly cares and the deceitfulness of riches choke it, leaving him unfruitful.

prompt.en: In the parable of the king settling accounts, why was the first servant finally handed to the tormentors?

text.en: He had no means of repaying the ten thousand talents he owed
He showed no mercy after his debt was forgiven
He hid his family’s wealth from the king while begging for patience
He complained to the king about what his fellow servants had done

explanation.en: The king forgave his huge debt, but the servant jailed a fellow servant over a far smaller one. The king then held him to account for showing no mercy.

prompt.en: What disagreement about worship did the Samaritan woman raise with Jesus?

text.en: Whether people ought to worship on her people’s mountain or in Jerusalem
Whether Samaritans were allowed to offer sacrifices at the temple in Jerusalem
Whether the Sabbath should be kept by Jews and Samaritans on the same day
Whether worship could rightly be offered at Jacob’s well instead of the temple

explanation.en: She said her fathers worshiped on this mountain, while Jews said Jerusalem was the place. Jesus answered that an hour was coming when neither would be the place.

prompt.en: When the disciples asked who had sinned, how did Jesus explain why the man was born blind?

text.en: His parents had sinned, and the consequence had fallen upon their son
He would be healed only when he confessed sins known to God alone
Neither had sinned; God’s works would be revealed in him
An evil spirit had bound him from birth and kept him from seeing

explanation.en: Jesus rejected both options the disciples offered, saying neither the man nor his parents had sinned, but that the works of God might be revealed in him.
